questions.stem: A 34-year-old with new hypertension is found to have renal artery stenosis. On this classification diagram, into which branch does her hypertension fall?

explanation.summary: Secondary hypertension (5-10% of cases) results from an identifiable cause such as renovascular, renal, or endocrine disease; primary hypertension has no identifiable cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: Secondary hypertension (5-10% of cases) results from an identifiable cause such as renovascular, renal, or endocrine disease; primary hypertension has no identifiable cause.

questions.stem: This hormonal cascade begins with hepatic angiotensinogen and raises blood pressure through vasoconstriction and renal sodium/water reabsorption. What is this system called?

explanation.summary: The diagram depicts the RAAS: renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, pulmonary ACE converts it to angiotensin II, which drives vasoconstriction and aldosterone-mediated Na/water retention.
explanation.whyCorrect: The diagram depicts the RAAS: renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, pulmonary ACE converts it to angiotensin II, which drives vasoconstriction and aldosterone-mediated Na/water retention.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a renal change leading to increased intravascular volume alongside vasoconstriction, together producing hypertension. Which renal event is depicted as the initiating step?

explanation.summary: Enhanced tubular Na+ reabsorption expands intravascular volume, which combined with vasoconstriction raises the product of SVR and cardiac output, elevating blood pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enhanced tubular Na+ reabsorption expands intravascular volume, which combined with vasoconstriction raises the product of SVR and cardiac output, elevating blood pressure.
